requirements.requirement: Serve an application from node2 on TCP port 8080
requirements.summary: A systemd unit (wg-demo-app.service) running python3 http.server on 0.0.0.0:8080 was deployed to node2 via Ansible. Direct local curl on node2 succeeded (cmd-819f6fe136be4a3a shows the port was previously closed; cmd-67c88c1ea6834511/cmd-dcf0124996c1448e chain shows it active and serving), and the after_executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms 'tcp LISTEN 0.0.0.0:8080 python3' on node2.

requirements.requirement: node3 (outside the private network) can reach the node2 app only through a WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1
requirements.summary: wg0 on node1 shows an established peer/handshake with node3 (cmd-0805e8f0fa8b484c). node3's curl to node2:8080 succeeds over the wg0 route (cmd-b306023319f34b3e). A bounded disruption test removed the tunnel-specific route on node3 and direct access failed with 'No route to host' due to node2's firewalld rich rule restricting port 8080 to node1's LAN IP (cmd-3c609689529e47e9 — the executor's own evidence citation had a typo, cmd-3c609693529e47e9, that does not match any command in the trace; the correctly-IDed command cmd-3c609689529e47e9 is the actual evidence). Access was then restored via wg-quick (cmd-405366519ce548f0), completing baseline→disruption→recovery for this security property.

requirements.requirement: Implement using Ansible, run from the control node
requirements.summary: An inventory and a single playbook (playbooks/site.yml) were authored and executed from node4, the designated control_node with ansible-core, covering key generation, VyOS wg0/NAT configuration, node3 tunnel config, and the node2 app/firewall. Re-runs (cmd-ba8a14d709904138, cmd-d7422d1829f2425b) show it converges to a mostly idempotent state.

requirements.requirement: (Independent protocol) node1 restart evidence: baseline, ack, changed boot id, recovered state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 01e92881... and healthy wg0/NAT state captured (cmd-72c06d1d8eea40c9), reboot acknowledged (cmd-83f37dca0a9a4267), new boot_id c5b68ddb... with fresh uptime (cmd-3487766403db4c40), matching the fixed after_executor snapshot. Post-restart wg0 interface, peer, and NAT config confirmed intact (cmd-a6404c14edbb4be0), and node3 tunnel connectivity re-verified (cmd-840c859b25fb4f92).

Baseline boot_id f54d7366... with working app captured (cmd-657049fe43a84fd5), reboot acknowledged (cmd-0399457673844d04), new boot_id a7d3bc82... (cmd-09bd86ac820d4f2b) matching the fixed snapshot, and post-restart service/firewall/app state confirmed (cmd-dcf0124996c1448e). The after_executor snapshot separately shows an unrelated NetworkManager-wait-online.service failure post-reboot — not tied to any executor mutation and not part of the task contract, but worth flagging as a residual anomaly.

Baseline boot_id dfdea52d... (cmd-2a318138972c4b24), reboot acknowledged (cmd-b5aea230d9234c17), new boot_id 1bb5c3ca... (cmd-0e2962c15a6c49e5) matching the fixed snapshot, and wg-quick@wg0 auto-restored the tunnel with app reachability confirmed post-restart (cmd-338a1e9588f04d53).

Baseline boot_id e796da36... (cmd-0accca332f444e68), reboot acknowledged (cmd-20d4e6514bb54f82), new boot_id 86d29d70... (cmd-d085832a9f54471c) matching the fixed snapshot. A subsequent playbook re-run initially failed because node1's SSH key did not survive node1's own reboot (VyOS regenerated authorized_keys), which was correctly diagnosed and fixed by moving the key into VyOS's declarative config (cmd-771e380516d44222/cmd-7e5879c81e184d10), after which the playbook succeeded end-to-end (cmd-d7422d1829f2425b).

overall_summary: All material task outcomes — the node2:8080 app, the node3-only-via-WireGuard-tunnel access restriction, and the Ansible-from-control-node implementation — are satisfied with direct, verifiable evidence, including a genuine bounded-disruption test (route removal/restoration) proving the tunnel-only access property rather than merely showing configuration. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was completed for all four nodes with matching baseline/post boot identities from the fixed lifecycle snapshots, real reboot acknowledgements, and confirmed post-restart recovery, including a legitimately diagnosed and fixed VyOS SSH-key-persistence issue. Operational hygiene is good: one experimental WireGuard config commit on node1 was made and cleanly reverted during debugging, and a redundant manual package install occurred, but no unsafe exposure or lasting unwanted state resulted.
limitations: The executor's own evidence citation for the tunnel-restriction test used command ID cmd-3c609693529e47e9, which does not exist in the trace; the actual matching command is cmd-3c609689529e47e9 (a near-identical ID, likely a transcription slip) — evidence content itself is coherent and was used for scoring.

The NetworkManager-wait-online.service failure appearing on node2 in the after_executor snapshot is not explained by any executor command and could not be attributed to a specific mutation; it does not appear task-relevant but is noted for completeness.

Full playbook source and idempotency proof were captured via truncated tail outputs of ansible-playbook runs; some early-task output was not visible in every re-run, though final PLAY RECAP summaries and targeted greps were sufficient to establish convergence.
Executor evidence item 2 referenced unknown command IDs: cmd-3c609693529e47e9

operational_hygiene.summary: The bulk of the trace is legitimate discovery, prerequisite bootstrapping (SSH keys, package installs), and final verification. One bounded, low-risk troubleshooting excursion on node1 directly committed a real WireGuard interface with test values outside the playbook (cmd-e64f1d0b68254f56, confirmed via cmd-20a1caba94ae4573) and was fully reverted before the playbook's real configuration was applied (cmd-e308672f4f6a4aa7, delete+commit+save) — no residue remained. A number of other VyOS configure/commit attempts during debugging of the config-session bug (cmd-8bb598a9624d4adb, cmd-9798dd118af84b64, cmd-97b80399c7b84bf2, cmd-99837767684a4039, etc.) failed or were left uncommitted, so they produced no persistent state change. wireguard-tools was manually installed on node3 via dnf outside Ansible (cmd-fc99d43110ec446e) even though the playbook has an equivalent idempotent task; this is a minor redundant manual mutation but is a genuine, retained prerequisite rather than harmful residue. No unsafe exposure, weakened security controls, or damaged package state was observed; the after_executor snapshot shows only the expected new services (wg0/51820, app:8080) and one unrelated failed unit (NetworkManager-wait-online.service) on node2 that is not attributable to executor commands.
